name: Ethereum

key_findings: Scored as L1 only, PoS era only -- all L2 rollup activity excluded from every metric.
Developer & Ecosystem (90), TradFi Approved (90), and Regulatory & Risk (90) are ETH's strongest categories -- deep institutional and builder penetration.

Privacy & Confidentiality (48) reflects a substantial privacy application ecosystem, roughly $4.2B cumulative through Railgun, zkBOB, and Tornado Cash, running on a base layer with no protocol-level confidentiality of its own. Aztec is excluded as a separate-security execution environment.
Quantum Resistance Partial cap (88) sits above the raw 80.78 and does not bind.
Raw 74.01 sits one point below the 75 Deterministic Finality Partial cap, so the cap does not bind.
Execution Layer (62) is dragged mainly by ~13-15 minute hard finality, a significant structural drag on settlement-dependent agent use cases.
KYA (83) is ETH's strongest AI category, driven by ERC-8004 being ETH's native, chain-agnostic identity standard.

The divergence between the two axes is broad-based, arising from three distinct structural weaknesses (slow finality, adversarial MEV/fee environment, weak L1 privacy) rather than one dominant gate wall.

watch_items: Post-Dencun burn collapse may warrant a Tokenomics revision from 80 toward 76-78 in a future re-assessment.
Fusaka/Glamsterdam roadmap items (single-slot finality, Verkle trees, PeerDAS) could materially shift Execution Layer if shipped.
